prize_parts.citation: for a visionary, densely patterned prose, rooted in poetry, that builds from memory, the body and dream an expansive metaphysical imaginary

statement.case_for: On public knowledge, Cărtărescu offers the most complete combination of the common criteria among the shortlisted writers. His voice is unmistakable: dense, rhythmically charged Romanian prose that grows out of his poetry. The Blinding trilogy and Solenoid are sustained architectures in which memory, the body, dream and cosmology are made into one imaginative universe, and they are not isolated virtuoso pieces. The formal ambition appears cumulative across several decades, and the later large-scale works look like an extension of the earlier concerns rather than a repetition. The imaginative and intellectual depth is considerable. His reception beyond Romanian culture suggests that the achievement carries across languages. This is a judgment about the whole body of work as it appears in public knowledge. I have not independently verified sources or read the texts for this stage.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the case rests heavily on translations of very dense, stylistically saturated Romanian prose, so the linguistic achievement, which is central to the claim, cannot be judged directly. The longest books may also be uneven. Encyclopedic excess and self-referentiality could count as a flaw as well as a strength, and sustained quality across the whole oeuvre, including the poetry and the earlier short fiction, is less well documented for me than the major novels. If the committee concludes that the late novels do not sustain their length, the case would weaken considerably.

responses.point: Mattson ranks Pierre Michon first for compressed, liturgical French prose that turns obscure lives and art history into narrative inquiry. She accepts that the slender corpus is a point for discussion, and she flags doubt about whether Cărtărescu's scale and self-referential density sustain their length.
responses.response: I share her view of Michon's sentence-level intensity and exactness, and it is why I keep him second. Where I differ is on breadth and on how much weight the 'whole oeuvre' framing can put on a small corpus whose effect depends so closely on the French sentence. I take her doubt about Cărtărescu's length seriously. It is the right test: whether the late books extend the project or merely enlarge it. From public knowledge I read them as extending it, but I cannot settle that without close reading, and I do not think the committee should treat it as settled.

responses.point: Swärd ranks Can Xue first for an uncompromising, anti-realist fiction whose formal radicalism is sustained over decades and is not a single-book effect. She notes that only part of the corpus is translated.
responses.response: I agree that Can Xue's voice is among the most original on the list, and I rank her third. My hesitation is the one Swärd herself names: the translated part of the corpus is partial, and a consistent dream-logic method makes it hard to show development and depth over time, as opposed to a recurring procedure. Cărtărescu's project has a cumulative architecture that shows more visibly how it grows. That difference is a judgment about what the evidence lets us demonstrate, not a verdict that her achievement is smaller. If colleagues can document development in her later work, I would reconsider.

responses.point: Olsson ranks Raúl Zurita first for a poetic project of rare formal and conceptual ambition that turns dictatorship-era suffering into collective memorial poetry, extended into landscape-scale interventions.
responses.response: The ambition and moral weight are real, and I do not want to discount them. My reservations are about what can be judged as literature. Poetry loses the most in translation, and part of the project's force lies in interventions known mainly through documentation. Olsson himself says the recognition of its historical significance should not stand in for literary judgment, and I agree. I would want the committee to be confident that the written sequences carry the case on their own before the preference moves to Zurita.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg also ranks Cărtărescu first, citing distinctiveness of voice and imaginative depth, while noting that the scale and density of the work may divide readers over sustained quality.
responses.response: I agree with his reading of the strengths, and I would keep his qualification in the record rather than let agreement on first place hide it. A shared ranking does not answer whether the density sustains quality across the long novels. That question needs more discussion with the translation uncertainty stated openly.

uncertainties: How much of Cărtărescu's linguistic achievement survives in translation is unresolved, because the case depends on dense, stylistically saturated Romanian prose that I cannot assess directly.
Whether the late, very long novels sustain quality and extend the earlier work, or enlarge it without deepening it, is not settled by public knowledge alone.
Coverage of the poetry, essays and earlier short fiction is thinner than that of the major novels, so the weight of the whole oeuvre is uncertain.

For Michon, the open question is whether a slender corpus meets the whole-oeuvre standard under Nobel's will; for Can Xue, whether development across a partly translated corpus can be shown. Both are unresolved.
No source was independently verified and no texts were read for this stage; all judgments rest on general public knowledge and the supplied committee documents.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. My own literary practice and my work on Selma Lagerlöf are context, not evidence of a connection to any shortlisted writer. The profile lists no tie to any shortlisted writer beyond ordinary committee colleagueship.
